shared_elements: shallow low-relief carving on coarse tan/buff stone
horizontal band or belt dividing the surface
row of repeated arch-like/rectangular units in the upper zone
curving linear motifs incised into the surface
justification: Both are monolithic blocks of pale, coarse stone whose surfaces are organised into stacked horizontal registers, with a repeated row of arch-like elements above, a banding line across the middle, and a prominent circular disc below — that register logic is the most specific correspondence. But A is a flat, crisply cut slab carrying an animal repertoire (birds in profile, a snake, a zigzag frieze) with no figural body, whereas B is a fully three-dimensional anthropomorphic figure with head, shoulders and arms, its motifs worn and much softer in cut, so the two read as entirely different objects.
